newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF to be sold under 1986 law.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF to be sold under 1986 law.

text.p: France's Council of State, the country's highest administrative court, has ruled that the sale of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF will be done under terms of the 1986 privatisation law, the finance minstry said on Friday.
"The Council of State has given its opinion to the Finance Ministry on the legal terms covering the transfer to the private sector of Thomson-CSF," the ministry said in a statement.
The court ruled that as Thomson-CSF constitutes an essential part of the assets of Thomson SA, the sale should be seen as a means of privatising the parent company, it said.
"Consequently, the privatisation of Thomson-CSF is covered, just as that of Thomson SA, by chapter II of the law of 6 August 1986 on privatisations," the ministry statement said.
The government intends to announce the sale terms for Thomson-CSF at the beginning of 1997, it said.

The court was asked to rule whether Thomson-CSF's sale was covered by the 1986 privatisation law or a 1991 decree which allowed state-owned companies to sell shares in their subsidiaries as a means of raising cash without a full privatisation.
The 1991 process allows a faster sale compared to the 1986 act, which requires the state to sell Thomson-CSF rather than than Thomson SA, which owns 58 percent of the defence unit.

The government suspended on December 4 the privatisation of Thomson SA through a private placement as the Privatisation Commission objected to the planned sale of consumer electronics firm Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea.
